key_insight: TRIAGE improves agent training by giving different actions different credit based on their role, instead of treating every token in a trajectory the same. This helps preserve useful exploration and reduces reinforcement of redundant or harmful actions.
problem_solved: It addresses the credit assignment problem in agentic reinforcement learning, where standard GRPO uses only the final outcome to score all action tokens equally. That makes it hard to learn from partial successes, exploratory moves, and action sequences with mixed quality.
method: Introduces a role-typed credit assignment framework that distinguishes environment-facing actions such as searches, clicks, edits, navigation, and object interactions.
Assigns credit more selectively so useful exploratory actions are not unfairly punished in failed rollouts.
Reduces over-rewarding of redundant or regressive actions in successful rollouts by aligning credit with action role and contribution.
impact: For practitioners, TRIAGE offers a more faithful training signal for agents that act in complex environments, which can improve learning stability and policy quality. It is especially relevant for web agents, embodied agents, and tool-using systems where not all actions contribute equally to success.

paper_title: TRIAGE: Role-Typed Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
